Field.Label: Read from IndigoSecrets.py first (MQTT_BROKER / MQTT_PORT / MQTT_USERNAME / MQTT_PASSWORD). Leave fields below blank if IndigoSecrets is set.
Broker Host:
Field.Description: Hostname or IP of your MQTT broker. Fallback only — IndigoSecrets.MQTT_BROKER takes precedence.

Field.Label: Topic Prefix:
Field.Description: The main zigbee2mqtt root topic. Must match your z2m config (usually "zigbee2mqtt").

Field.Label: Garage Topic Prefix:
Field.Description: Optional second Z2M instance topic prefix (e.g. "zigbee2mqtt_garage"). Leave blank to disable.

Field.Label: Seconds of MQTT silence before the liveness watchdog probes (and, if unanswered, rebuilds) the connection. Raise this on a small/quiet Zigbee network. Minimum 60.
Log Routine Activity to the Event Log

Off by default. Routine narration - command echoes such as 'sent "Hall Lamp" set brightness to 40%', status requests, device announcements and the MQTT connect steps - is written only to this plugin's own log file (Indigo's Logs folder, com.clives.indigoplugin.z2mbridge/plugin.log). Indigo does not log a state change of its own for these devices, so the echo is the only record that a command went out - that record is not lost, it just lives in this plugin's log rather than the shared one, which is where you would look anyway if a light had not responded. Tick this to send the narration to the Event Log as well; "Show Debug Info in Event Log" below does the same and adds the debug detail on top. Warnings and errors always appear in the Event Log whatever these are set to.
